When origin does not contain the selected local commit, Boat cannot fetch it for exact-commit seeding if the source capsule exposes that commit as its transport HEAD. The existing full-file fallback preserves correctness but loses the seeded transfer path.

## User Impact

Boat can seed from the captured base while the verified source capsule still supplies the selected local commit, dirty bytes, deletions and file modes to the payload.

## Why This Change Was Made

After source selection, candidate index and bundle creation, the Boat caller selects the captured base as the disposable transport HEAD before staging is sealed. Original source identity, witness, candidate tree and carrier remain intact. Other providers and native Crabbox admission are unchanged; an unavailable captured base retains the existing fetch/fallback behavior.

Current candidate `230dc74bc4a86264fbb8a43d146cae4ab8c7a0c2` integrates the frozen main baseline `2ab28a6bcb5cc3ecc9d221b3c964de771a17e491`. The parent dependency, https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191845, has merged.

- The real wrapper/receiver regression failed against the original producer because native-boundary capture saw the origin-absent source commit instead of the base. It passed at original candidate `7739efb0d637314359bc004e96c6ea9eab61e45c` (one selected test; 311 skipped).

Root and independent review found no issues in the current contribution. Native preparation is `github_pending`; hosted CI supplies broader current-head validation.

- Released Crabbox **0.83.0** completed a real Boat wrapper run from an unpublished local commit with a dirty overlay. The payload verified the selected source witness, a distinct carrier rooted at the captured base, dirty content, executable mode, deletion and an unchanged control file. It exited 0, released its workspace owner and left local HEAD/index/dirty content unchanged. issue.body:
Related: #193163
Related: #196154
Follow-up to #193190

## What Problem This Solves

`openclaw update` can spend minutes running candidate validation before refusing at `database-engine-preflight` when a PostgreSQL Gateway holds state ownership and the updater will not stop it.

## User Impact

Refuse before canary validation with the existing ownership reason and next step, preserving the installation and running Gateway. Runtime retention and candidate installation still occur first. Managed services the updater will stop, separately parked foreground updates, stopped Gateways and SQLite-only installs retain their behavior.

## Why This Change Was Made

The existing preactivation probe protects the installation, but runs after validation. Reuse it at the candidate-validation owner boundary when neither a future managed stop nor foreground park can release ownership. Keep the final probe for an owner that starts later. Keep the probe inside the validation error boundary so package installs retain `database-engine-preflight` rather than `global-install-failed`.

Maintainer correction `f8d69b280dd8de97718898bbd5e73d19c2b10194` passes the managed exemption only when `shouldRestart` is true. A running owned or unresolved service under `--no-restart` therefore refuses early. The foreground parking exemption remains separate.

Full PR production delta: +45 net lines for this early ownership boundary; correction production delta: 0. Tests: +188, allocated in the task's own test-line record; shared cap unchanged. No schema, auth, restart-policy, cancellation or capture-durability change.

## Evidence

- Exact signed head: `f8d69b280dd8de97718898bbd5e73d19c2b10194`.
- Independent full-range source review resolved its sole old-index finding by staging the explicitly reviewed correction. A later fixture-only field completes the existing owned-service verdict type; no unresolved source finding. Bounded independent final proof review found the runtime gap resolved.
- [Required exact-head CI](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42880149636): completed success. CI's build job was skipped; it is not counted as build proof.
- Fresh Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01m73e8gxsc0atpmskka05jv9s`, [allocation run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/42883663446), exact head verified: `update-command-execution.test.ts`, `update-command-foreground.test.ts` and `update-command-candidate-validation.test.ts` all passed, 102 tests in 3 files (77.91 s).
- Full `pnpm build` passed on that exact source; installed CLI reports `OpenClaw 2026.11.2 (f8d69b2)`. The build also reported CSS/chat-boot budget warnings; no claim that every asset budget passed. The PR changes only update CLI source/tests and its allocation record.
- Formatting, diff checks and signed commit hooks passed. Original author evidence (179 tests, red/green controls and a stable-package/Git PostgreSQL upgrade trace) remains historical; it does not substitute for corrected-head proof.

## Corrected-head installed CLI behavior

On the same isolated Linux Testbox, the canonical package helper produced and installed the exact-head package into a separate npm prefix. A uniquely named canonical profile was installed through the real user-systemd owner with PostgreSQL 17, a file SecretRef and normal token auth.

The repository's existing `packFirstHopUpdateFixture` produced a distinct `2026.11.3-first-hop.0` candidate from that package. Its complete member-digest receipt changed only `package.json`, `dist/build-info.json` and `dist/postinstall-content-inventory.json`; compiled runtime bytes were unchanged. An earlier identical-artifact run correctly returned already-current and is excluded from defect proof.

Actual installed entry point:

```text
openclaw --profile <isolated-profile> update \
  --tag file:<candidate-next.tgz> --yes --no-restart --json
exit=1 status=error reason=database-engine-preflight elapsed=55.911s
steps=updater-runtime-retention, package-install, package-update, gateway recovery observation
candidate canary validation steps=none
```

Preliminary candidate admission ran; canary snapshot/Doctor/lint/config/plugins/recovery/Gateway validation did not. Before and after refusal:

- All 24,042 hashed core package files were unchanged.
- Native service PID, process start identity and systemd start timestamp were identical.
- Authenticated Gateway RPC and HTTP readiness succeeded.
- PostgreSQL marker data was unchanged.

Native installation initially refused the runner's existing world-writable ancestor. Only the absent private service directories were created; existing permissions, manager configuration and the guard were unchanged.

## Review follow-through and limits

The [previous exact-head review](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196157#issuecomment-6747186690) had zero source findings and required the installed managed PostgreSQL `--no-restart` proof above. That proof is now complete. Native preparation, enforced checks and landing remain required.

`openclaw update` can spend minutes running candidate validation before refusing at `database-engine-preflight` when a PostgreSQL Gateway holds state ownership and the updater will not stop it.

The existing preactivation probe protects the installation, but runs after validation. Existing startup preflight prepares the empty store; an independent native PostgreSQL query requires its webhook migration completion before seeding. Parent workers drain before ownership passes to each real Gateway. Restart advances only the Gateway clock past the queue lease, so platform lease reclaim is outside this proof.

Extends [worker ACK-response-loss coverage](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/196111) to a full Gateway crash before ACK executes. A requester notice could prematurely fail a paused subagent and lose a retained send after plugin reload. Behavior bug (incorrect output/state without crash)

Successful resumed staging should satisfy the same descriptor admission requirement as fresh staging. Copy verification alone should not certify admission.

Grounded control: fresh staging invokes the real admission check and rejects this exact metadata state.

Baseline resume returns success despite continued admission failure. The real CLI `stageMaterialize` caller converts successful stage return into `ownerAdmitted: true`.

A local workaround reruns admission, returns its failure and preserves the anchor file. The test verifies the anchor-file SHA256, not the entirety of PostgreSQL contents.

2026.11.5-beta.1; SHA512-verified unmodified npm release

Ubuntu 24.04.4 LTS, x86_64; Node.js 24.22.1; PostgreSQL 17.11

Isolated extraction of the official npm tarball

Synthetic fixtures and private PostgreSQL UNIX socket. No production databases, credentials or conversations.

```text
baseline fresh stage: metadata admission error
baseline resume: success
baseline subsequent descriptor admission: same error
workaround resume: same admission error
workaround anchor-file SHA256: unchanged
```

Scripts and results: `runtime-tests/migration/`, especially `ports.mjs` and `baseline/port-results.json`.

https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/36a1c58e91dd9ae991edd76f9ccbfdcd056c5fa0/src/infra/database-engine/port-command.worker.ts

Later copy/catalog verification is not equivalent to descriptor admission. Full CLI orchestration and its later failure paths were not executed.

Related: #188956, #190129 (this PR removes the repeated read snapshots inside one history page, a measured part of the #188956 latency; #190129 addresses the worker queueing in front of it)

## What Problem This Solves

On PostgreSQL, some `chat.history` pages open a new read-only transaction for each step of the page read instead of one: a sparse page (few visible replies among many silent ones) takes three `BEGIN ... READ ONLY` / `ROLLBACK` round trips over the database bridge, and a Claude CLI session after a provider switch takes seven. When the database is across a network hop, every extra round trip adds to the page's response time.

## User Impact

User impact: each `chat.history` page on PostgreSQL is read from one database snapshot. Sparse pages and Claude CLI sessions after a provider switch now take one transaction for the page instead of three or seven, which makes those pages faster when PostgreSQL is not on loopback: with about 3.4 ms added round trip, median latency drops by 14 to 26 ms for a sparse page and about 40 ms for a Claude CLI session after a provider switch (see Evidence). Pages that already took one transaction are unchanged. Returned messages and pagination are unchanged, and SQLite is unchanged.

## Why This Change Was Made

The history worker runs one task at a time, and no read snapshot outlives a task. The `chat.history` page task now holds one PostgreSQL `REPEATABLE READ READ ONLY` snapshot from its first read until the page is assembled. That covers the Claude CLI import check (revision read and, after a provider switch, its tail read) and every page and tail-scan read. Every read still goes through the read scope's admission (`acquire`), so validation and path checks run per read as before. A failed read rolls the held snapshot back and the next read opens a fresh one. A failed rollback retires the connection, as `runPostgresTransactionSync` does, and the snapshot uses the same `BEGIN` and read-snapshot scope.

Scope: this changes the page task only. The pending-input read that the handler issues before the page is its own worker request with its own snapshot, and the history reader cap (#169110) is untouched. It keeps the eager read-only `BEGIN` (the deferred `BEGIN` in #188952 was closed unmerged).

Scope question for review: this is a partial fix of #188956, so it keeps `Related:` instead of `Closes`. Options: (a) land this on its own and keep #188956 open for the worker queueing in #190129; (b) fold both into one PR; (c) hold this until #190129 lands. Recommended: (a). Whichever of this and #190129 lands second switches to `Closes #188956`. The two changes touch different files, each is measured on its own, and this one already removes 2 or 6 read-only transactions (4 or 12 round trips) per affected page with no other behavior change.

issue.body:
Related: #189815

## What Problem This Solves

WhatsApp is missing the `edit` message action that Telegram and Discord have, so an agent cannot correct a message it already sent.

## User Impact

User impact: agents can edit their own WhatsApp messages. Turn it off with `channels.whatsapp.actions.editMessage: false`.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds `edit` the same way `react` works, behind the host's exact-current chat gate. Editing another user's message is refused when the cache knows the sender. On a cache miss the edit goes out under the bot's own key (`fromMe: true`); WhatsApp applies an edit only when it comes from the original sender, so such an edit has no effect on the other phone. That is provider behaviour, not something this PR enforces. Baileys resolves on the socket write, so the result says `submitted: true, confirmed: false`.

The edit key's chat is pinned to the chat the caller named. The message-cache lookup that quoting uses also matches a message through its sender. Only an entry whose stored peer number is the target's own number counts as this one-to-one chat under its other JID (phone number or LID) and may supply the key's `remoteJid`; anything else (a status update keyed by its poster, a broadcast list, a match through a bare participant JID) is another chat, and the edit is rejected with `message belongs to another chat`.

Caller authority: `edit` is declared in `writeAuthorityActions`, and the host's `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` is passed down the edit chain as a plain parameter. It is checked at the action handler and again inside the queued socket task, right after the socket-identity check and right before the native `sendMessage`. An edit whose originating run lost authority while it waited in the per-socket queue is dropped before any I/O. A revocation is never retried: the caller guard runs at the start of every send attempt, also while the socket is away, so a revoked caller never waits for a reconnect backoff, and the retry path re-checks the caller before classifying an error as a disconnect, so the caller gets the original guard error. Edits now use the ordinary send path, so the separate single-attempt path is gone.

Provider ownership (`fromMe`, the message cache) only scopes which messages are eligible; it does not stand in for caller authority. Both are required.

Scheduled edits stay out on purpose: `edit` is not in `providerOwnedReadGates`, so the host keeps its exact-current chat check and rejects a scheduled edit. A contract test locks that.

Known limitation: for an external install the host compares targets literally (it applies `normalizeTarget` only to bundled plugins), so a delegated edit must name a DM as `+E164`, the spelling the agent's prompt shows, or omit the target; a `...@s.whatsapp.net` spelling is rejected, fail-closed. Changing that is host policy and out of scope here.

## Evidence

### Live proof on 2026.11.1 (latest stable)

**Upgrade.** A real linked WhatsApp install was upgraded from 2026.10.10 to 2026.11.1 with the normal npm install, `plugins update` and `doctor --fix`. Before and after the upgrade, the full config (sorted JSON), the WhatsApp auth creds and the number of files in the WhatsApp auth dir hashed identically, and the cron list count was unchanged. The channel came back `linked, connected, health:healthy` and the agent answered on its primary model. The config has no `actions.editMessage` key.

**Edit.** Then this PR's commit was cherry-picked onto `v2026.11.1`, `extensions/whatsapp` was packed with `scripts/plugin-npm-publish.sh --pack`, and only the plugin's `dist` + manifest were swapped in (same dependency versions; all 94 `plugin-sdk/*` imports exist in the installed 11.1 core). Afterwards the stock 2026.11.1 plugin was put back. The cherry-pick differs from this branch only where 11.1's file layout differs from main (the action list lives in `channel-actions.ts` there, plus import lines); the edit, authority and socket code is the same as the pushed head, including the final same-chat guard and the no-socket caller check.

Phone number redacted; the message id is a random WhatsApp id.

```text
$ openclaw --version
OpenClaw 2026.11.1 (4ffdd20)

$ openclaw message send --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 3"
"action": "send", "handledBy": "core", "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8"
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "Proof test for the WhatsApp edit action: meet at 4"
"action": "edit", "handledBy": "plugin",
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8" }
[exit 0]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +15555550100 --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message "must not arrive"
ToolAuthorizationError: WhatsApp edit blocked: chatJid "+15555550100" is not in the
configured allowFrom list for account "default".
[exit 1]

$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8 --json \
    --message ""
Error: WhatsApp edit rejected: text is empty.
[exit 1]

# a message the other phone sent earlier; after the restart the cache does not know it
$ openclaw message edit --channel whatsapp --target +<owner> --message-id 3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A --json \
    --message "must not arrive (not this account's message)"
"payload": { "ok": true, "submitted": true, "confirmed": false, "messageId": "3A7E5B8528B197B3CF6A" }
[exit 0]
```

**Receiving side.** On the receiving account's WhatsApp Web (read-only IndexedDB lookup by message id), the received message `3EB0C0887D06069C093CA8` carries `latestEditMsgKey`, with the edit's sender timestamp 4.4 s after the original. So the edit reached the other phone; it is not only a socket write. The last command above targets a message the other phone itself sent: the socket accepted the write (`submitted: true`), but on the receiving side that message has no `latestEditMsgKey`. WhatsApp dropped the edit because it did not come from the message's sender, which is the provider behaviour the Why section relies on for a cache miss.


### Delegated edit from a real inbound turn (2026.11.1)

Same install and plugin port, plugin installed under `~/.openclaw/extensions` (origin `global`, so the host treats it as an external plugin, the same trust class as the integration test below). The owner's phone sent the bot a WhatsApp DM asking it to call the `message` tool twice. The group is configured and allowed (`groups` + `groupAllowFrom`, the bot is a member), so the plugin itself would accept it. Gateway log plus the session trajectory from `openclaw sessions export-trajectory`; numbers redacted, times UTC:

```text
14:19:11  CLI (direct operator)  message send -> +<owner>  messageId 3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19  "...: meet at 3"
14:19:43  web-inbound            Inbound message +<owner> -> <bot> (direct, 494 chars)
14:19:49.724  tool.call  message  {"action":"edit","channel":"whatsapp","target":"+<owner>",
                                   "messageId":"3EB0982B3059BFDD8B7B19","message":"...: meet at 4"}
```

Not covered live: a second linked account and revocation while queued (one linked account; revocation cannot be timed from outside). Both are covered by the host-issued-guard integration test below.

- Host-issued caller guard, end to end (`test/whatsapp-message-edit.integration.test.ts`, on the shared `createMessageReadAuthority` harness, reaching the plugin only through `api.js` and a new `extensions/whatsapp/test-api.ts`, the same public test surface the Discord and Slack suites use): a really minted turn capability and run claim, the message tool under the gateway caller identity, the in-process `message.action` handler (which builds `assertDirectAdapterHandoff` itself), the plugin registered as an external install, the real WhatsApp handler and the real socket session; only Baileys' `sendMessage` is a mock.   1. the current chat's edit reaches the socket with the edit key and returns `submitted: true, confirmed: false`;
  2. the same run naming another allowed chat is rejected before the socket;
  3. the same run's identity sent straight to the gateway's `message.action` with another allowed account is rejected by the host before the socket;

- Contract: a scheduled `whatsapp:edit` is rejected with "requires provider-owned target authorization".

- Upgrade compatibility: a config without `actions.editMessage` parses and enables edit; the message cache is in memory and its shape is unchanged.
